title: Judge shard windows on log-precision step times and say when a short window is decided
body:
Outcome: the shard wall report's slowest-step verdict uses sub-second step times and says whether a short window is already decided, so the lead acts on a window as soon as its verdict cannot change.
Evidence: GitHub's jobs API keeps whole seconds: Test (7/10) of run 42446730414 reads 04:25:30Z to 04:25:50Z (20 s) while its log spans 04:25:30.94 to 04:25:50.63 (19.7 s). Over all 100 Test jobs of the 10 newest main runs at 183dcf3, |api - log| reached 0.9 s, and at e9ebc8f the slowest p50 read 19 s from the API but 19.3 s from the logs, so a p50 within 1 s of the 18 s target can flip on truncation. At 183dcf3, node scripts/shard-wall-report.mjs --since e79cb01 printed 'runs: 3 of 5 wanted since e79cb01' and FAIL at a 20 s p50 with every slowest step at 20-21 s: the 5-run median is already at least 20 s, yet the line reads like a FAIL that two more runs could reverse, because slowestVerdict judges whatever runs it has.
Acceptance: testStepSeconds prefers logStepSeconds and uses the API timing only when the log lacks the step. While used < wanted the verdict ends 'decided' when more than wanted/2 slowest steps sit on one side of the target (a PASS also needs no untimed step) and 'provisional' otherwise; tests cover both at 3 of 5. Live, --since e79cb01 prints a decided FAIL.
